## Licensing (strict, and enforced by the build not by memory)

Learned the expensive way on Telegraph: we published competition binaries under MIT,
and MIT is precisely the permission to take a registered artifact, append a few bytes
that rescale its output, and register the result as a rival entry. Twelve scorer slots
were taken from us that way, every one decoding to our own base plus a two-band map,
and every one of those takings was lawful. A miner deployment (`livecert`) was found
running our answer templates too. None of that is a complaint about anyone's conduct;
it is a correction of our own licence choice, and these rules exist so the choice is
never made carelessly again.

### 1. Default outbound licence: source-available, no derivatives

Anything we publish that competes on a public leaderboard, or that a rival can fetch
and re-register, ships under **Source-Available No-Derivatives** (SPDX
`LicenseRef-zkasuran-SAND-1.0`), not MIT. The reference text is
`work/telegraph/scorer/LICENSE`; copy it, do not re-draft it.

It grants what a reader, validator or judge needs and nothing more: run it for any
purpose including commercially, read it, decompile it, benchmark it, publish what you
find. It withholds exactly one thing, redistribution and derivative works, because
that is the thing that was used against us.

MIT (or Apache-2.0 where a program demands a patent grant) is correct for a genuine
upstream contribution: a PR into someone else's repo takes that repo's licence, and a
standalone library meant to be adopted wants adoption. The test is whether the artifact
is a **contribution** or an **entry**. Contributions get permissive terms. Entries get
SAND.

### 2. The licence goes in the bytes

A binary fetched from a raw URL arrives with no `LICENSE`, no `NOTICE` and no README, so
terms that live only in a repository are terms the holder never sees. Put them inside
the artifact:

- wasm: an inert custom section (`work/telegraph/scorer/rev/stamp.py`). The runtime
  ignores custom sections, so behaviour and exports are unchanged and `strings x.wasm`
  shows the terms.
- other binaries: an equivalent inert region, or a sidecar the fetch instructions name.
- source, JSON descriptors, YAML: an SPDX header line.

Make the pipeline refuse, rather than trusting anyone to remember. `reg_batch.py` will
not register an unstamped file without an explicit `--allow-unstamped`, and that is the
pattern to copy: **the publish step verifies the licence, or the publish step is wrong.**

### 3. Upstream first when the artifact is mostly someone else's

When a build's bulk is another author's work reused under their licence, their terms
govern those portions and ours cover only our addition. Say so **before** our own
notice, in the bytes, so a reader who only runs `strings` still lands on the right
licence. `stamp.py --upstream URL --upstream-licence SPDX --upstream-copyright LINE`
does this, and it refuses a URL given without both the licence and the copyright line:
naming a source without its terms is worse than not naming it.

### 4. Lineage is read off the bytes, never hand-maintained

`PROVENANCE.json` is generated (`rev/provenance.py`) by fingerprinting every published
file and grouping each build with its base, so the record cannot drift from what is
actually published. Three states, and only three:

| lineage | meaning | licence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `own` | our source, our build | SAND-1.0 |
| `source_fork` | built from another author's **source** under a licence permitting it | theirs, named, plus ours on our addition |
| `binary_wrap` | another author's **compiled binary** plus our bytes | not publishable |

`binary_wrap` must read zero. If one appears, the file is withdrawn, recorded in
`WITHDRAWN.json` with the reason, and it stays withdrawn even when it would win. We
withdrew 44 such files on 2026-08-30 and that decision is not reopened because a slot
is close.

### 5. Every third-party input needs a quotable clause

Before any data source, model weight, font, image or audio track enters a build, read
its terms and record the exact granting sentence in the lane's `DATA-SOURCES.md`. If
the grant cannot be quoted the source does not ship, and the answer says what is
missing rather than serving something we may not republish.

Two verdicts from the Telegraph audit worth carrying forward, because they are the
shapes that catch people out:

- "Free API" is not a licence. Open-Meteo's free tier is non-commercial only, so it
  came out of every miner and was replaced with MET Norway (CC BY 4.0 + NLOD 2.0) and
  the US NWS ("free to use for any purpose"). A rival still running open-meteo is on
  the wrong side of a clause we already moved off.
- No stated licence at all means no permission to redistribute a modified copy. Absence
  of terms is not permission.

Attribution that a licence requires is not optional and is not "framing": CC BY, ODbL
and MIT all require it, and the credit goes where a user of the artifact sees it.

### 6. Licence changes are dated, bounded and irrevocable backwards

A licence change never claws anything back. Record the boundary commit, state which
grant covers which period, and say plainly that anyone who obtained a copy under the
old terms keeps them and owes nothing.
`work/telegraph/scorer/LICENSE-HISTORY.md` is the template.

### 7. Before any repo flips public

Check, in this order: `LICENSE` present and correct for entry-vs-contribution;
`NOTICE` naming every third-party component with its own terms; `PROVENANCE.json`
regenerated with `binary_wrap: 0`; every published binary carrying its section
(`stamp.py --check` returns clean); `DATA-SOURCES.md` quoting a clause per source;
and no private-data file (`submit/`, form fills, keys) tracked. A public repo is a
publication, and a publication with the wrong licence cannot be un-published.

## Storage management (measure, repack, then delete, in that order)

Learned on 2026-09-03, when the 483G root hit 95% full with 25G left. A 23-area audit
reclaimed 222G. The single biggest win was not a deletion. This section is the whole rule.
It complements **Reuse before rebuilding** in step 2 of the method: that one says do not pay
for an install twice, this one says do not keep what nobody will read again.

### Trigger and order

Above 85% on `/`, reclaim. Below that, leave it alone and spend the turns on lanes.

Always in this order, cheapest and most reversible first: measure, repack, delete. Start with
`df -h /` and `du -xm --max-depth=5 /home/asuran | sort -rn | head -40`. Get the whole
inventory before touching anything. A reclaim that starts with an `rm` is a reclaim that
deletes the wrong thing.

### Repack before deleting anything

Run `git count-objects -v` on every repo over a few hundred MB. A large `size:` with
`in-pack: 0` means loose objects, which get zlib but no delta compression, so every
historical version of every blob is stored whole.

`work/telegraph/scorer` held 3363 loose objects at 15,681 MB because `dist/` is tracked and
holds ~1769 near-identical 29 MB wasm blobs. A plain `git gc` took `.git` to 1,076 MB. That
is 14.6G freed with nothing deleted, nothing to re-download, on a repo carrying 257 dirty
files that no `rm` is allowed near. `scorer-lab` had the same disease at smaller scale.

Use plain `git gc`, not `--prune=now`, so the default two-week window keeps recent
unreachable objects. Sweep for this before proposing a single deletion.

### What makes a tree disposable

All four, not three: an origin remote, a clean `git status --porcelain`, an empty
`git log --branches --not --remotes`, an empty `git stash list`. Miss one and the tree holds
work that exists nowhere else.

Stale remote-tracking refs overstate the unpushed count. teleworld reported 176 of 198
worktrees carrying unique work and the true answer was none, because those counts came from
refs that had never been fetched. Confirm against the live remote before believing a big
number. See [[teleworld-local-state-is-disposable]].

Worktree branches live in the main repo's `.git`, provable with
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, so `git worktree remove` destroys only uncommitted content
and never a commit. Commit the dirty ones first, then remove the directories with
`git worktree remove --force` so the metadata goes too.

### Extract, then delete

When a large tree is kept only for a small amount of unique work, take the work out rather
than keeping the tree.

- Tracked changes: commit them on their own branch, then `git format-patch -1` into the lane.
  The patch carries its parent SHA, so `git am` refuses on a wrong base instead of misapplying.
- Untracked files: copy them to the lane root, beside the results they produced.
- Write a `RESTORE-*.md` naming the clone URL, the base SHA, the apply step plus any
  submodule init the build needs.
- Verify with `git apply --check --reverse` before the `rm`. Gate the `rm` on the saved file
  existing and being non-empty.

On 2026-09-03 `3mdeb-lane/902/coreboot` (1,881 MB) and `tenstorrent/build/tt-metal` (719 MB)
were held by 69 and 124 lines respectively. Both trees went, both changes survive as a patch
and a file.

### Never delete

- Everything protected by **Licensing** and the FLOP spec: `../flop/work/flop/identity/`, any key,
  `.passphrase` or `.env*`, any `submit/`, any `DEMO-*.mp4` or `upload-*/`, packets and state
  docs, `PROVENANCE.json` with the bytes it fingerprints.
- Any repo with no origin remote. `work/bond` is the standing example and gets its
  `node_modules` taken and nothing else. See [[bond-lane-has-no-remote]].
- `~/.config/google-chrome`. It holds the live login cookies that headless work copies.
- A live lane's inputs. A dataset counts as regenerable only when the exact download command
  can be named. If it cannot be named, it is irreplaceable whatever its size, which is why
  `work/virtual-embryo/external/jax` keeps 10.1G.
- A model cache that a script opens with `local_files_only=True`. Deleting that is a hard
  failure, not a silent re-download.

### Measure honestly

Hardlink farms double count: `.cache/uv` into every venv, `.cargo/git/db` into `checkouts`,
mamba `pkgs` into `envs`. Run `du -csm` over the pair for the real gain.

Trust the `df` delta, never the sum of per-path `du`. The 2026-09-03 per-path sum predicted
202G where the real figure was 185G.

Some trees resist `rm` inside home. `go/pkg/mod` needs `go clean -modcache`. NuGet caches
plus waydroid data are root-owned. sudo has no password in session, so `/var` work (journal,
snapd, logs, swapfile) is a handoff with exact commands, not a blocked step.

### Leave a record

Write the vetted paths to `work/RECLAIM-<date>.txt` before running them, then keep the file.

Once a lane's deadline has passed and its outcome is recorded in the tracker, its build
artifacts are fair game. Clearing them then is cheaper than an emergency sweep at 95%. The
full account of what was freed, what stays and why is in [[reclaim-disk-space-audit]].

## MiniMax (Max plan, through ~2026-12-18) — default AI provider for submission builds

For the next 3 months every submission build that needs an LLM, text-to-speech or reasoning uses the
MiniMax Max plan by default. OpenAI-compatible, one Bearer key. This supplements the house LLM gateway
rule for submission-building work; where a program forbids a given provider, follow the program.

* **Base URL:** `https://api.minimax.io/v1` (mirror `https://api.minimaxi.chat/v1`). Auth header
  `Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_API_KEY`.
* **Key:** `MINIMAX_API_KEY` in `~/Downloads/hackathon-hq/.minimax.env`, mode 600. Never in a repo,
  never printed, never pasted into a PR, issue, form or chat. Source at point of use:
  `set -a && . ~/Downloads/hackathon-hq/.minimax.env && set +a`.
* **Text / reasoning:** `MiniMax-M3` (flagship, reasoning — emits `<think>...</think>` then the answer),
  plus `MiniMax-M2.7 / M2.5 / M2.1` and their `-highspeed` variants for cheaper, faster calls. Chat via
  OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` or native `/v1/text/chatcompletion_v2`.
* **Voice (TTS):** `POST /v1/t2a_v2`, model `speech-02-hd` (or `speech-01`). No GroupId needed on this
  key. Returns `data.audio` as a HEX string of an mp3 (decode hex to bytes). Use for demo-video narration.
* **Music:** NOT on this key (410, "no longer available to new users"). Keep using the house
  no-copyright track for videos.
* Verified 2026-09-18: /v1/models, chat, and t2a all 200; music 410.

## Tooling

Lane-specific rules live in that lane's own `CLAUDE.md` and override the general habits
here where they conflict. `work/virtual-embryo/CLAUDE.md` is the live example: on a scored
leaderboard the goal is rank, so only point-scale jumps count and a confirmed knob gets
swept at x2 to x3 spacing until the board turns over before anything new is built.

- `gh auth status` (zkasuran should be active)
- `gh pr view <N> --repo <repo> --comments`
- `gh pr checks <N> --repo <repo>`
- `gh pr create --repo <upstream> --base main --head zkasuran:<branch> --title ... --body-file ...`
- Post a comment or set a PR body from a file with `-F body=@<file>`, never `-f`.
  `-f` sends the string literally, so `-f body=@reply.md` posts the text `@reply.md`
  and you have to delete the comment and repost. `gh pr edit --body` is a silent
  no-op on these repos, so PATCH a body over REST:
  `gh api -X PATCH repos/<O>/<R>/pulls/<n> -F body=@<file>` and verify the live body.
  See memory `gh-pr-edit-body-fails-use-rest`.
- Run the project's own commands: `pytest`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`,
  `mypy`, or whatever the repo uses. Match the repo, not a default.

### Looking at images: never read anything over 2000 px

The image reader refuses any image whose longest edge is over 2000 px once a conversation already
holds many images. The refusal is not a skipped picture: it fails the whole turn and the work stops.
Screenshots taken at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` come out 2100 to 2500 px wide, so they trip it every time.
On 2026-10-05 a README art check died mid-task this way.

- **Never pass an original screenshot to the reader.** Make a review copy first and read that:
  `python3 bin/preview-image.py <file.png> [more.png ...]`. It writes `/tmp/preview/<dir>-<name>.png`
  with the longest edge at most 1800 px and prints the path. `--max` lowers it further.
- **SVG is not readable as an image at all.** Render it to PNG first with a headless Chrome
  screenshot at its own size (1280 wide for the README art), then preview that.
- **Read at most four images per call.** Preview only the ones that answer the question. Every
  image read stays in the conversation and counts toward the many-image limit.
- **Keep shipping files at 2x.** The limit applies to what is read for review, never to what is
  published. Downscale the copy, not the asset.

## Disclosure template (adapt per PR)

> AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) was used in developing this change. The
> design, review and verification were done by the author. Verified locally
> before submitting: <the tests/lint/type-checks that pass>.

Keep prose clean and specific. Lead with the author's ownership. The AI line is
a brief factual note, not the headline. Do not overclaim what the human reviewed;
state what was actually verified.

## Writing style (PR text, comments, docs, commit messages)

Write like a human, not an AI. This is about voice only. It does not change
principle 2: the AI disclosure stays. Clean human prose plus an honest
disclosure is the goal, not hiding that AI helped.

Write it clean from the first token. These rules are a drafting habit, not a
cleanup pass. Hold them in mind as the text is written rather than emitting AI
prose and scrubbing it after: the scrub wastes turns (each is $0.10) and a slip
that reaches a reviewer costs a whole round. Every subagent brief that produces
outward words puts these rules at the top, framed as "do not emit these", not
"fix these later".

- No em dashes. Use a comma, a period, parentheses or a rewrite instead.
- No comma before "and" or "or". No Oxford comma, and no comma-before-and habit.
- No AI tells or filler. Drop "it's worth noting", "in conclusion", "delve",
  "robust", "seamless", "leverage", forced three-item lists, throat-clearing
  and hedging.
- Short direct sentences. Plain words. Vary the length so it reads natural.
- Say what changed and why. Skip the marketing voice.

Applies to every outward word: PR titles and bodies, issue and review comments,
commit messages and docs.

**The gate is a command now, not a habit.** `bin/voice-gate.mjs` checks em dashes,
comma-before-and and the AI tells above, and `bin/portal-post.sh` runs it before any
request leaves the machine and refuses to POST on a hit. Use `portal-post.sh` for
dashboard updates and mentor replies rather than hand-rolling curl.

    node bin/voice-gate.mjs body.txt
    PORTAL_SESSION=... bin/portal-post.sh reply <question-id> body.txt

This exists because on 2026-09-25 I posted an update and four mentor replies without
running the grep: 15 em dashes and 18 comma-before-and went out. The update was
revisable. **The mentor replies were not.** `PATCH` and `PUT` on a reply both return
404, so no edit route exists, and an answered question returns 409
`INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`. Those four replies are permanent. Deliberate exceptions
take `voice-gate:allow` on the line, or a `voice-gate:off` / `voice-gate:on` fence for
quoted text such as verbatim licence wording.

One pre-send gate, because these models drift back to em dashes and Oxford commas
in long output no matter the instruction. A #42 comment once went out with 14
comma-before-and slips despite the rule. Before posting anything outward, grep the
text for em dashes and for `, and` / `, or` and fix any hit. Treat it like a linter
over code you already meant to write clean: an empty result is the expected state,
not a surprise, and it is not the mechanism, the clean drafting is. Upstream
template wording quoted inside our PR body (the checklist lines) is theirs, leave
those commas alone.

## Frame the work as our own

Our designs, docs and outputs present our own ideas in our own voice. They are
not a literature review of who we borrowed from, and not a derivative of prior
work dressed up with citations. State the idea plainly as ours.

Do not scatter inline references through the body: no file-and-line pointers to
our own prior builds, no "adapted from", "lifted from" or "ported from", no
naming another platform as the source of a design choice. Our prior work is ours
already, so it needs no citation. Experience is a strength to state, not a
reference to attach.

Give explicit credit only where something demands it. A source license that
requires attribution gets it. A platform or program that requires disclosure gets
it, and the AI disclosure in principle 2 is exactly that kind of demand and it
stays. Absent a demand, our voice and our design.

This is framing, not dishonesty. The honesty floor does not move: never state an
external fact we have not verified as settled (a contract address, an ABI, a
third-party parameter), and never claim a human reviewed what no human read.
Internal tracking notes, a lane ledger or a reuse comment we keep for our own
benefit, are not outward credit and are fine.

## Resume

On "continue" or a new session: read `START-HERE.md`, check live PR status, then open
Hackathon HQ for the full reminder feed: `node work/hq/hq.mjs remind` for the digest or
`node work/hq/hq.mjs serve` for the dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:7788. HQ is the
consolidated view over deadlines, winner-announcement checks, PRs and bounties in one
place, sharing the same store as the opportunity tracker (`node work/opps/opps.mjs due`
is the narrower deadline-and-recheck slice of it). HQ records each project's
lifecycle phase on its own through SessionStart and Stop hooks that run `hq scan`,
so progress from building through finished, submitted, deadline passed and winner
day writes itself down with nothing to hand-maintain. Respond to any maintainer activity,
then pick the next target and triage it live (dedupe first with
`node work/opps/opps.mjs check`, record the verdict with `opps add` or `opps set`; set a
lane's outcome once results land with `node work/hq/hq.mjs results`).
Operate under **Execution authority** and **Content cadence** above for every
target, the same way, from the first action of the session. On anything touching
flop-labs, technocore.chat or $FLOP, `../flop/CLAUDE.md` applies from the first
commit, not at submit time.

</system-reminder>

House rules: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Lane rules: .hq/CLAUDE.md. Read both first.

neatHack entry (neatlogs AI-agent hackathon, 10-12 Oct 2026). Building PriorProof:
a prove-or-refuse prior-authorization agent. Chosen by zkasuran from a 9-lens
brainstorm on 2026-10-10. Submission = public GitHub repo + demo video, announced
by quote-tweeting neatlogs on X. Hard deadline 2026-10-12 23:55 IST (18:25 UTC).
Winners 2026-10-16.

Input: a real public payer medical-necessity policy + a synthetic patient chart
(NO PHI, ever). Output: a submission-ready prior-auth packet + a criterion-by-
criterion coverage matrix where every criterion is EITHER proven against a cited
span in the chart OR left red and returned as a named gap. Core invariant: the
agent never greens a criterion it cannot cite. Two independent passes
(policy->record and record->policy) must agree on the same cited span before green.

agent 30, use of neatlogs+Entire+cfo.ai 25, demo video 20, building in public 15,
usefulness+originality 10. Build to all five.

  provider-agnostic (swap ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a Vercel env var to use Claude).
  ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3034 is the local gateway for THIS session
  only, NOT reachable from a deployed Vercel function, so never bake it into the app.

  the integrations with graceful degradation (local trace store when no neatlogs
  key) and hand off the signups/keys to the human.

  Telegraph wording for PriorProof-neutral. Never MIT (house rule 6).

  anonymous (house repo-visibility rule).

   CLI/checkpoint; cfo.ai business plan + prior-auth cost figures; landing.md IA.

Operator setting fan-out width. Then fire the research wave.

A prove-or-refuse prior-authorization agent for neatHack. The one invariant that
defines the product: the agent proves each medical-necessity criterion against a
cited span in the chart, or leaves it red and returns it as a named gap. It NEVER
fabricates support for a criterion.

## Hard constraints
- NO PHI. Real public payer policy + synthetic chart only. Label "synthetic" in the
  product and the README.
- Host on Vercel. Never bake the localhost gateway URL into the app.
- Mandatory stack (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai) must be intrinsic, not bolted on, and
  must degrade gracefully when a key is absent so the demo always runs.
- Prove-or-refuse is a tested invariant: an adversarial test feeds a chart missing a
  criterion and asserts it stays red. Mutate the engine to prove the test can fail
  (LESSONS: prove your check can fail).

## Build / test / lint (fill as set)
- pnpm install; pnpm typecheck; pnpm lint; pnpm test; pnpm build
- One release gate: ./verify.sh (typecheck + lint warnings-as-errors + tests +
  build + audit at 0). CI runs the same script.

## Rubric
agent 30, stack 25, demo 20, build-in-public 15, usefulness/originality 10.

## Decisions
- 2026-10-10: chose PriorProof from the brainstorm. Vercel host (operator call). App
  LLM OpenAI now, provider-agnostic client. Licence SAND-1.0 (reuse hailjury).

R6 handles the Next.js/Vercel architecture: serverless routes with streaming for the live coverage matrix, env vars, CSP headers via vercel.json, and function timeout limits. That gives six research tasks total, which fits comfortably within the width-8 parallel limit, so I'll keep all six as planned rather than splitting R1.

Reconsidering R1 though — it's the foundation everything else builds on, so I want it to pick a genuinely public policy with clean enumerated criteria, possibly surveying a few candidates before committing to one and justifying the choice, plus authoring the synthetic chart. Each agent needs a full brief covering context, specific task, scope boundaries, and the outward-words style note where relevant since some outputs may eventually feed into public-facing content.

I'm also setting shared ground rules: research agents stay read-only and return findings as text rather than writing files, which avoids conflicts with the build agents that actually create files. For R2/R3/R4 which need web and docs reading, I'll lean toward general-purpose since it's built for complex research with full tool access, though I'm checking whether it still inherits CLAUDE.md like the catch-all claude type does.

I need to spell out the core invariant that a criterion only turns green when two independent passes (policy-to-record and record-to-policy) agree on the same cited chart span, and that these are pure research tasks returning raw findings for the orchestrator -- no file writes, with sources cited and unconfirmed items flagged.

input.prompt:
Context: We are building PriorProof for neatHack, a 48-hour AI-agent hackathon by neatlogs (10-12 Oct 2026). PriorProof is a prove-or-refuse prior-authorization agent. Given a real public payer medical-necessity policy and a synthetic patient chart (no PHI), it assembles a submission-ready prior-auth packet plus a coverage matrix where every medical-necessity criterion is either proven against a cited span in the chart or left red and returned as a named gap. Core invariant: it never greens a criterion it cannot cite. This is a research task: your returned text IS the deliverable (raw data for the orchestrator). Do NOT write files. Findings will be verified before use, so cite sources (name + URL) and flag anything you could not confirm.

Your task is the data foundation everything else builds on. Do two things:

1) Choose ONE real, publicly available payer medical-necessity policy that is (a) genuinely public with a working link, (b) enumerates clear checkable medical-necessity criteria (ideally a numbered list of required findings), and (c) makes a good demo: 6 to 12 criteria including at least one that needs a specific documented history (for example "failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy"). Strong sources: CMS National or Local Coverage Determinations (NCD/LCD) on cms.gov, or a public commercial medical policy (UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna). A common, well-defined procedure (for example lumbar MRI for low back pain, or a specific surgery or imaging study) works best. Return: the policy name, the payer, the exact public URL, and the ORDERED list of criteria with the EXACT policy wording for each.

2) AUTHOR a realistic synthetic patient chart (NO PHI, fully fictional names and dates) for a plausible patient seeking that service, written like real clinical notes (chief complaint, HPI, exam, imaging, prior treatments, medications, relevant history). It must SATISFY most criteria with specific documented facts, and leave exactly ONE important criterion unsupported (the refusal-demo gap). Return the full chart text, then a mapping table: each criterion -> supported yes/no -> the exact quotable chart sentence that supports it, or "GAP: not documented" for the one gap. Make supported sentences short and quotable so an engine can cite a span. Keep it medically plausible but obviously fictional.

Be precise and complete. This defines the whole demo.

input.prompt:
Context: We are building PriorProof for neatHack, a 48-hour AI-agent hackathon by neatlogs (10-12 Oct 2026). PriorProof is a prove-or-refuse prior-authorization agent: given a payer medical-necessity policy and a patient chart, it proves each criterion against a cited span or leaves it red as a named gap, and assembles a submission-ready prior-auth packet. cfo.ai is a mandatory tool: a business-planning agent (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) whose output goes in the submission. This is a research + drafting task: your returned text IS the deliverable. Do NOT write files. Cite every external figure (source name + URL) and flag anything you could not confirm.

Two parts:

1) Find how cfo.ai is meant to be used for neatHack (cfo.ai/neathacks) and what artifact it produces. Note the signup caveat (a card is required, cancel immediately in Settings -> Billing to avoid being billed). Keep this short.

2) DRAFT the PriorProof business plan, grounded in REAL US prior-authorization figures. Research primary sources (AMA prior authorization physician survey, CAQH Index, KFF, CMS, HHS OIG) for: annual prior-auth volume, average physician and staff time and cost per prior auth, denial rate, appeal rate, overturn-on-appeal rate, and the cost of a denial. - The buyer (provider groups, revenue-cycle-management firms, billing companies, specialty practices).
- Pricing (a per-packet fee and/or a per-seat SaaS tier) with a defensible number.
- COGS: LLM API spend per packet (assume a few model calls per criterion), hosting on Vercel.
- Gross margin, break-even packets per month, and a simple 12-month revenue and runway sketch for a solo founder.
- The value anchor: staff hours saved and denials avoided per the real figures.

Return the full plan as structured text (sections with headers and the key numbers in bold). Follow house outward-words style in the prose: no em dashes, no comma before "and" or "or", no filler words like "robust" or "seamless" or "leverage", short direct sentences. 1	<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-zkasuran-SAND-1.0 -->
2	# Hail Jury security model
3	
4	## What each party could try, and what stops it
5	
6	| Attacker | Attack | Defence | Where |
7	|---|---|---|---|
8	| Seller | Read bids early with their own "beacon" key | Any manifest whose drand chain is not League of Entropy quicknet (hash, key, genesis, period, scheme) is rejected | `drand.rs` `is_trusted` |
9	| Seller | Change terms after bids arrive | Bids bind to the auction id, which is a hash of the terms, in both the memo prefix and the AEAD key. Edited terms make every bid unopenable, and the audit fails the `manifest` check | `bid.rs`, `audit.rs` |
10	| Seller | Act as a guardian | Seller key may not equal a guardian key | `manifest.rs` |
11	| Guardian | Drop a bid they saw | Bid ids are published on the sealed board while bidding is open. A missing one fails `sealed_board` | `audit.rs` |
12	| Guardian | Shave a refund, pick a favourite, misprice | Settlement is a pure function of public inputs. Any change fails `transcript` | `settle.rs` |
13	| Guardian | Sign alone | Requires a threshold of distinct listed guardians. Duplicate and outsider signatures do not count | `audit.rs` |
14	| Anyone | Fake beacon | BLS pairing check against the chain key. The relay must also answer the round that was asked for | `drand.rs`, `drand.ts`, CLI |
15	| Bidder | Bid after the reveal | Late if mined above `close_height` or at or after the reveal time. Refunded, never counted. The CLI refuses to build such a bid | `settle.rs`, CLI |
16	| Bidder | Replay a memo into another auction | Auction-id prefix plus AEAD binding | `bid.rs` |
17	| Bidder | Replay a memo in the same auction | Counted once, then `duplicate` and refunded | `settle.rs` |
18	| Bidder | Seal to a different round | The memo header round must equal the reveal round | `bid.rs` `open_at` |
19	| Anyone | Crash settlement with a junk memo or ledger | No panics in non-test code (clippy `deny(unwrap_used, expect_used, panic)`). Property tests feed random bytes to every parser | `tests/adversarial.rs` |
20	| Anyone | Exhaust memory or CPU | Ceilings: 100k notes, 512-byte memos, string lengths, guardian and attestation counts, 256 MB CLI input, 64 KB relay responses, 15 s relay timeout | `lib.rs` `limits`, CLI |
21	| Anyone | Count one note twice by changing case or padding | Ledger rows are normalised (lower-cased, memo re-padded) before deduplication | `ledger.rs` |
22	| Local user | Read a secret from `ps` | Seeds come only from `--seed-file` (with a permission check) or `HAILJURY_SEED`, never argv | CLI |
23	| Web attacker | Script injection | Strict CSP: `default-src 'none'`, scripts limited to self plus a hash, `connect-src` limited to the drand relays, no `object-src` or `base-uri`. `_headers` adds `frame-ancestors 'none'`, nosniff and HSTS. Rendered JSON and code are escaped | `vite.config.ts`, `public/_headers` |
24	| Web attacker | Tampered localStorage or showcase file | Sandbox rooms are re-verified (seller signature) on load. Showcase bundles must pass a full audit before they render | `store.ts` |
25	
26	## Known limits
27	
28	- **Guardians see deposit values.** A deposit shows a ceiling on the bid, bucketed to 1, 2 or 5 × 10^k.
29	- **Refund addresses become public in the transcript.** Use a fresh diversified address per bid.
30	- **The audit proves misconduct but cannot reverse a payment.** Custody is only as good as the FROST quorum.
31	- **The audit does not prove the ledger is complete or that payouts happened.** That needs a chain scan with the escrow UFVK.
32	- **The showcase and sandbox use a simulated ledger and sandbox addresses.** No ZEC moves.

# Hail Jury security model

## What each party could try, and what stops it

| Attacker | Attack | Defence | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seller | Read bids early with their own "beacon" key | Any manifest whose drand chain is not League of Entropy quicknet (hash, key, genesis, period, scheme) is rejected | `drand.rs` `is_trusted` |
| Seller | Change terms after bids arrive | Bids bind to the auction id, which is a hash of the terms, in both the memo prefix and the AEAD key. Edited terms make every bid unopenable, and the audit fails the `manifest` check | `bid.rs`, `audit.rs` |
| Seller | Act as a guardian | Seller key may not equal a guardian key | `manifest.rs` |
| Guardian | Drop a bid they saw | Bid ids are published on the sealed board while bidding is open. A missing one fails `sealed_board` | `audit.rs` |
| Guardian | Shave a refund, pick a favourite, misprice | Settlement is a pure function of public inputs. Any change fails `transcript` | `settle.rs` |
| Guardian | Sign alone | Requires a threshold of distinct listed guardians. Duplicate and outsider signatures do not count | `audit.rs` |
| Anyone | Fake beacon | BLS pairing check against the chain key. The relay must also answer the round that was asked for | `drand.rs`, `drand.ts`, CLI |
| Bidder | Bid after the reveal | Late if mined above `close_height` or at or after the reveal time. Refunded, never counted. The CLI refuses to build such a bid | `settle.rs`, CLI |
| Bidder | Replay a memo into another auction | Auction-id prefix plus AEAD binding | `bid.rs` |
| Bidder | Replay a memo in the same auction | Counted once, then `duplicate` and refunded | `settle.rs` |
| Bidder | Seal to a different round | The memo header round must equal the reveal round | `bid.rs` `open_at` |
| Anyone | Crash settlement with a junk memo or ledger | No panics in non-test code (clippy `deny(unwrap_used, expect_used, panic)`). Property tests feed random bytes to every parser | `tests/adversarial.rs` |
| Anyone | Exhaust memory or CPU | Ceilings: 100k notes, 512-byte memos, string lengths, guardian and attestation counts, 256 MB CLI input, 64 KB relay responses, 15 s relay timeout | `lib.rs` `limits`, CLI |
| Anyone | Count one note twice by changing case or padding | Ledger rows are normalised (lower-cased, memo re-padded) before deduplication | `ledger.rs` |
| Local user | Read a secret from `ps` | Seeds come only from `--seed-file` (with a permission check) or `HAILJURY_SEED`, never argv | CLI |
| Web attacker | Script injection | Strict CSP: `default-src 'none'`, scripts limited to self plus a hash, `connect-src` limited to the drand relays, no `object-src` or `base-uri`. `_headers` adds `frame-ancestors 'none'`, nosniff and HSTS. Rendered JSON and code are escaped | `vite.config.ts`, `public/_headers` |
| Web attacker | Tampered localStorage or showcase file | Sandbox rooms are re-verified (seller signature) on load. Showcase bundles must pass a full audit before they render | `store.ts` |

## Known limits

- **Guardians see deposit values.** A deposit shows a ceiling on the bid, bucketed to 1, 2 or 5 × 10^k.
- **Refund addresses become public in the transcript.** Use a fresh diversified address per bid.
- **The audit proves misconduct but cannot reverse a payment.** Custody is only as good as the FROST quorum.
- **The audit does not prove the ledger is complete or that payouts happened.** That needs a chain scan with the escrow UFVK.
- **The showcase and sandbox use a simulated ledger and sandbox addresses.** No ZEC moves.
- **Sandbox tickets and guardian seeds sit in this browser's localStorage, unencrypted.** They are demo keys only.

## Supply chain

- Every direct dependency is pinned (`=x.y.z` in Rust, exact versions in npm), and both lockfiles are committed.
- `cargo audit` and `npm audit` report 0 known vulnerabilities.
- `cargo deny` checks licences, sources (crates.io only) and wildcards.
- The licence travels inside the shipped wasm as a custom `license` section. The build fails if it is missing.

Run `./verify.sh` for the full gate.

# PriorProof on Next.js + Vercel — build-ready architecture

Confirmation legend: **[DOC]** verified against official docs just now, **[INF]** inferred/best-practice (reasoning given), **[FLAG]** could not confirm or has a version caveat.

---

## 1. Project structure

The engine is a pure async-generator library under `lib/engine` with zero `next/*` and zero `process.env` reads. The route handler injects an LLM client into it and adapts its yielded events to SSE. Fixtures are TS modules (not loose files) so Vercel's build tracer always bundles them into the function **[INF — on serverless, `import` guarantees inclusion; `fs.readFile` of an arbitrary path is only included if the tracer sees it, so prefer imports]**.

```
priorproof/
├── app/
│   ├── layout.tsx                 # root layout, reads nonce from headers() for <Script> if needed
│   ├── page.tsx                   # server component shell; renders <CoverageMatrix/> island
│   ├── globals.css
│   └── api/
│       └── run/
│           └── route.ts           # POST → SSE stream.  runtime='nodejs', maxDuration=300
├── components/
│   ├── CoverageMatrix.tsx         # 'use client' — opens the stream, fills live
│   ├── CriterionRow.tsx           # one row: two evidence passes + verdict
│   └── PacketView.tsx             # final prove/refuse packet
├── lib/
│   ├── engine/                    # PURE, importable, unit-testable without a server
│   │   ├── index.ts               # runEngine(): AsyncGenerator<EngineEvent>
│   │   ├── parse.ts               # policy text → Criterion[]
│   │   ├── evidence.ts            # two independent passes per criterion
│   │   ├── decide.ts              # prove-or-refuse from the two passes
│   │   ├── packet.ts              # assemble the packet
│   │   └── types.ts               # Criterion, Verdict, EngineEvent, LlmClient
│   ├── llm/
│   │   ├── client.ts              # getLlmClient() — picks provider from env (server-only)
│   │   ├── openai.ts
│   │   └── anthropic.ts
│   ├── fixtures/
│   │   ├── index.ts               # loadCase(id) → { policy, chart }
│   │   └── cases/
│   │       └── knee-mri.ts        # synthetic policy + synthetic chart, typed objects
│   └── sse.ts                     # encodeSse() / parseSse() shared helpers
├── __tests__/
│   └── engine.test.ts             # feeds runEngine a FAKE LlmClient, asserts event sequence
├── proxy.ts                       # Next 16 nonce CSP + per-request security (see §5)
├── next.config.ts                 # static security headers (§5)
├── vercel.json                    # optional: default function maxDuration
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json
```

Boundary rule that satisfies "engine stays pure": `getLlmClient()` reads env and lives in `lib/llm`; the engine receives it as `deps.llm` and never imports it. Tests pass a fake.

```ts
// lib/engine/types.ts
export type Criterion = { id: string; text: string }
export type Verdict = 'prove' | 'refuse'
export interface LlmClient {
  complete(a: { system: string; prompt: string; json?: boolean }): Promise<string>
}
export type EngineEvent =
  | { type: 'criteria_parsed'; criteria: Criterion[] }
  | { type: 'criterion_start'; id: string }
  | { type: 'evidence'; id: string; pass: 1 | 2; found: boolean; cite?: string }
  | { type: 'criterion_resolved'; id: string; verdict: Verdict; rationale: string }
  | { type: 'packet_ready'; packet: unknown }

// lib/engine/index.ts  — NO next/*, NO process.env
import type { EngineEvent, LlmClient } from './types'
export async function* runEngine(
  input: { policy: string; chart: string },
  deps: { llm: LlmClient; maxCriteria?: number },
): AsyncGenerator<EngineEvent> {
  let criteria = await parseCriteria(input.policy, deps.llm)
  if (deps.maxCriteria) criteria = criteria.slice(0, deps.maxCriteria) // demo cap
  yield { type: 'criteria_parsed', criteria }
  for (const c of criteria) {
    yield { type: 'criterion_start', id: c.id }
    const [a, b] = await Promise.all([            // two independent passes, parallel
      findEvidence(c, input.chart, deps.llm),
      findEvidence(c, input.chart, deps.llm),
    ])
    yield { type: 'evidence', id: c.id, pass: 1, found: a.found, cite: a.cite }
    yield { type: 'evidence', id: c.id, pass: 2, found: b.found, cite: b.cite }
    const d = decide(a, b)
    yield { type: 'criterion_resolved', id: c.id, verdict: d.verdict, rationale: d.why }
  }
  yield { type: 'packet_ready', packet: assemble(/* collected */) }
}
```

---

## 2. Server-side run + live streaming

Use a **Route Handler returning a `ReadableStream`, framed as Server-Sent Events**, not a Server Action. **[DOC]** route handlers stream by returning `new Response(stream)` where `stream` is a `ReadableStream`, and the docs show exactly the async-iterator-to-stream pattern (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route, "Streaming"). Server Actions are RPC-style and return a single buffered result; React can stream action values via `createStreamableValue` (AI SDK), but that couples you to React internals. A route handler + SSE is portable, needs no extra dependency, and lets a plain `fetch` reader fill the matrix **[INF — portability/dependency judgment]**.

Why SSE over `EventSource`: `EventSource` is GET-only. PriorProof POSTs a `caseId` (and could POST a whole chart), so consume the stream with `fetch` + `response.body.getReader()` instead **[INF]**.

```ts
// app/api/run/route.ts
export const runtime = 'nodejs'   // LLM SDKs + maxDuration export + fluid-compute budget  [DOC]
export const maxDuration = 300    // seconds; see §4 for why 300 is the safe ceiling          [DOC]

import { runEngine } from '@/lib/engine'
import { getLlmClient } from '@/lib/llm/client'
import { loadCase } from '@/lib/fixtures'

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { caseId } = await req.json()
  const input = loadCase(caseId)
  const llm = getLlmClient()                     // reads OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  const enc = new TextEncoder()

  const stream = new ReadableStream({
    async start(controller) {
      const send = (event: string, data: unknown) =>
        controller.enqueue(enc.encode(`event: ${event}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(data)}\n\n`))
      // heartbeat: docs warn HTTP/1.1 intermediaries can drop an idle connection  [DOC]
      const hb = setInterval(() => controller.enqueue(enc.encode(`: ping\n\n`)), 15000)
      try {
        for await (const ev of runEngine(input, { llm, maxCriteria: 12 })) send(ev.type, ev)
        send('done', { ok: true })
      } catch (err) {
        send('error', { message: (err as Error).message })
      } finally {
        clearInterval(hb)
        controller.close()
      }
    },
  })

  return new Response(stream, {
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8',
      'Cache-Control': 'no-cache, no-transform',   // no-transform discourages proxy buffering [INF]
      'Connection': 'keep-alive',
      'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no',                    // belt-and-suspenders against buffering     [INF]
    },
  })
}
```

Client (a `'use client'` component) — the matrix fills as each `criterion_resolved` arrives:

```ts
// components/CoverageMatrix.tsx (excerpt)
async function runCase(caseId: string, onEvent: (e: {event: string; data: any}) => void) {
  const res = await fetch('/api/run', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ caseId }),
  })
  const reader = res.body!.getReader()
  const dec = new TextDecoder()
  let buf = ''
  for (;;) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read()
    if (done) break
    buf += dec.decode(value, { stream: true })
    const frames = buf.split('\n\n'); buf = frames.pop() ?? ''
    for (const f of frames) {
      const event = f.match(/^event: (.*)$/m)?.[1]
      const data  = f.match(/^data: (.*)$/m)?.[1]
      if (!event || !data) continue          // skip ": ping" heartbeats
      onEvent({ event, data: JSON.parse(data) })
    }
  }
}
// setState on each event → React re-renders the row for that criterion id → live fill
```

---

## 3. Env vars on Vercel (server-only secrets)

Any variable **without** the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix is server-only and never enters the browser bundle **[DOC — Next.js env var semantics]**. So `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` stay secret by simply not prefixing them. Never read them in a `'use client'` file; read them only in `lib/llm/client.ts` and the route handler.

Setting them with the CLI (project already linked, authenticated as zkasuran) **[DOC — https://vercel.com/docs/cli/env, updated 2026-08-20]**:

```bash
# interactive (prompts for the value, hides it from shell history)
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production
vercel env add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY production      # optional provider
vercel env add NEATLOGS_API_KEY production

# non-interactive, explicitly a Secret, no prompt
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production --sensitive --value "sk-..." --yes

# from a file as the value (keeps the secret out of bash history — preferred over `echo |`)
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production < ./openai.key

vercel env ls                                     # verify what is set, per environment
```

Add to `preview` too if you demo from a preview URL. Production vars default to type `secret` **[DOC]**. The docs explicitly warn that `echo value | vercel env add` saves the value in bash history, so use the interactive prompt or `< file` for keys **[DOC]**.

For local dev, pull them into an untracked file **[DOC]**:
```bash
vercel env pull .env.local            # development env by default
```

---

## 4. Timeout limits and keeping the agent under them

**[DOC — https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/duration, updated 2026-08-24]**, with Fluid compute (enabled by default on new projects):

| Plan | Default | Maximum | Extended |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hobby | 300s | **300s (5 min)** | — |
| Pro | 300s | **800s** | 1800s (30 min), beta |
| Enterprise | 300s | 800s | 1800s, beta |

Configured in App Router with the named export `export const maxDuration = 300` in the route file **[DOC]**.

**[FLAG]** these numbers assume Fluid compute is on (it is the default). If Fluid compute is disabled on the project, the older/shorter serverless limits apply and the agent can get cut off mid-run. Confirm Fluid compute is on in Project → Settings before the demo.

The limit that bites a live demo is the Hobby 300s ceiling, plus the docs' own warning that **idle** HTTP/1.1 connections can be dropped by intermediaries. Mitigations, in priority order:

1. **Stream incrementally (primary).** TTFB is tiny because `criteria_parsed` emits almost immediately and every `criterion_resolved` is pushed the instant it resolves. The matrix is visibly filling long before the function would ever hit its ceiling, so even a slow total run reads as "working," not "hung."
2. **Heartbeat every ~15s** (`: ping` comment frames) so an idle stretch between LLM calls does not look idle to the network **[DOC rationale]**.
3. **Cap criteria** for the demo (`maxCriteria: 12`). Bounds worst-case wall-clock.
4. **Parallelize the two evidence passes** per criterion with `Promise.all` (already in the sketch) to roughly halve per-criterion latency.
5. **Per-call timeout + global budget [INF].** Give each LLM call an `AbortController` timeout (e.g. 25s) and track a soft budget; if the budget is nearly spent, emit remaining criteria as a `deferred` verdict rather than blocking past the function ceiling.
6. Keep `runtime='nodejs'`. Edge runtime has different, shorter constraints and the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs expect Node **[INF; I did not pull exact Edge limits — [FLAG]]**.

Set a project-wide default in `vercel.json` if you prefer not to annotate each route **[DOC]**:
```json
{ "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "functions": { "app/api/**/*": { "maxDuration": 300 } } }
```

---

## 5. Content-Security-Policy and security headers (Next production)

landing.md's Vite plugin does not apply. The Next-native approach is a **nonce-based CSP generated per request in the proxy/middleware file**, with the static (non-nonce) headers in `next.config`. **[DOC — https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy, Next 16.4.0]**

**[FLAG — file name is version-dependent]** On **Next 16** the file is **`proxy.ts`** exporting `proxy()` (this is what `create-next-app` scaffolds in Oct 2026, and what the current docs show). On **Next 13.4–15** it is **`middleware.ts`** exporting `middleware()`, with an identical body. Rename the file and the function; nothing else changes.

**Tradeoff to accept consciously [DOC]:** a nonce forces **dynamic rendering** on every page (no static optimization, no CDN caching, PPR incompatible), because the nonce is injected during SSR from the request's CSP header. For PriorProof this is fine, the app is an interactive live demo, not a cacheable marketing page. If you later need the landing page statically cached, the alternative is Next's experimental hash-based CSP via Subresource Integrity (`experimental.sri`) which keeps static generation **[DOC]**.

```ts
// proxy.ts  (Next 16;  rename to middleware.ts / middleware() on <=15)
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'

export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64')
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'
  const csp = `
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ''};
    style-src 'self' ${isDev ? "'unsafe-inline'" : `'nonce-${nonce}'`};
    img-src 'self' blob: data:;
    font-src 'self';
    connect-src 'self';
    object-src 'none';
    base-uri 'self';
    form-action 'self';
    frame-ancestors 'none';
    upgrade-insecure-requests;
  `.replace(/\s{2,}/g, ' ').trim()

  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers)
  requestHeaders.set('x-nonce', nonce)
  requestHeaders.set('Content-Security-Policy', csp)
  const res = NextResponse.next({ request: { headers: requestHeaders } })
  res.headers.set('Content-Security-Policy', csp)
  return res
}

export const config = {
  matcher: [{
    source: '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)',
    missing: [
      { type: 'header', key: 'next-router-prefetch' },
      { type: 'header', key: 'purpose', value: 'prefetch' },
    ],
  }],
}
```

Notes: `connect-src 'self'` explicitly allows the same-origin `fetch('/api/run')` stream (it would also fall back to `default-src 'self'`). The matcher deliberately excludes `/api`, so the CSP's nonce machinery never touches the SSE endpoint (which returns `text/event-stream`, not HTML) — correct. Next auto-attaches the nonce to its own framework scripts and to `<Script nonce={nonce}>` read via `headers()` **[DOC]**.

Static headers (apply to every response including `/api` and static assets) go in `next.config` — do **not** also put CSP here, to avoid a conflicting second policy:

```ts
// next.config.ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
const securityHeaders = [
  { key: 'X-Content-Type-Options', value: 'nosniff' },
  { key: 'Referrer-Policy', value: 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' },
  { key: 'X-Frame-Options', value: 'DENY' },                 // legacy clickjacking fallback; frame-ancestors 'none' is the modern one in the CSP
  { key: 'Strict-Transport-Security', value: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' },
  { key: 'Permissions-Policy', value: 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), browsing-topics=()' },
  { key: 'X-DNS-Prefetch-Control', value: 'off' },
]
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  async headers() {
    return [{ source: '/:path*', headers: securityHeaders }]
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```

**[INF]** HSTS `preload` is only appropriate once you are certain the apex and all subdomains are HTTPS-only; on a throwaway `*.vercel.app` demo you may drop `preload`. Vercel serves HTTPS and sets HSTS on its own domains anyway.

---

## 6. Deploy commands (CLI already authenticated as zkasuran)

**[DOC — https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli, updated 2026-09-08]**

```bash
# 1. link this directory to a Vercel project (creates .vercel/)
vercel link

# 2. attach secrets BEFORE deploy (see §3), then confirm
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production
vercel env add NEATLOGS_API_KEY production
vercel env ls

# 3. pull project settings + env locally so a local build matches prod
vercel pull --environment=production      # writes to .vercel/

# 4a. simple path — build on Vercel and promote to production
vercel --prod

# 4b. or prebuilt path — build locally, inspect .vercel/output, then upload
vercel build
vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod
```

**[DOC]** the first deploy of a brand-new project is always a production deploy even without `--prod`; later deploys need `--prod` to hit production (otherwise they are preview). `vercel pull` (not `vercel env pull`) is the one to use alongside `vercel build`/`vercel dev` because it writes both settings and env into `.vercel/` **[DOC]**.

# PriorProof on Next.js + Vercel — build-ready architecture

Confirmation legend: **[DOC]** verified against official docs just now, **[INF]** inferred/best-practice (reasoning given), **[FLAG]** could not confirm or has a version caveat.

## 1. Project structure

The engine is a pure async-generator library under `lib/engine` with zero `next/*` and zero `process.env` reads. The route handler injects an LLM client into it and adapts its yielded events to SSE. Fixtures are TS modules (not loose files) so Vercel's build tracer always bundles them into the function **[INF — on serverless, `import` guarantees inclusion; `fs.readFile` of an arbitrary path is only included if the tracer sees it, so prefer imports]**.

```
priorproof/
├── app/
│   ├── layout.tsx                 # root layout, reads nonce from headers() for <Script> if needed
│   ├── page.tsx                   # server component shell; renders <CoverageMatrix/> island
│   ├── globals.css
│   └── api/
│       └── run/
│           └── route.ts           # POST → SSE stream.  runtime='nodejs', maxDuration=300
├── components/
│   ├── CoverageMatrix.tsx         # 'use client' — opens the stream, fills live
│   ├── CriterionRow.tsx           # one row: two evidence passes + verdict
│   └── PacketView.tsx             # final prove/refuse packet
├── lib/
│   ├── engine/                    # PURE, importable, unit-testable without a server
│   │   ├── index.ts               # runEngine(): AsyncGenerator<EngineEvent>
│   │   ├── parse.ts               # policy text → Criterion[]
│   │   ├── evidence.ts            # two independent passes per criterion
│   │   ├── decide.ts              # prove-or-refuse from the two passes
│   │   ├── packet.ts              # assemble the packet
│   │   └── types.ts               # Criterion, Verdict, EngineEvent, LlmClient
│   ├── llm/
│   │   ├── client.ts              # getLlmClient() — picks provider from env (server-only)
│   │   ├── openai.ts
│   │   └── anthropic.ts
│   ├── fixtures/
│   │   ├── index.ts               # loadCase(id) → { policy, chart }
│   │   └── cases/
│   │       └── knee-mri.ts        # synthetic policy + synthetic chart, typed objects
│   └── sse.ts                     # encodeSse() / parseSse() shared helpers
├── __tests__/
│   └── engine.test.ts             # feeds runEngine a FAKE LlmClient, asserts event sequence
├── proxy.ts                       # Next 16 nonce CSP + per-request security (see §5)
├── next.config.ts                 # static security headers (§5)

├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json
```

Boundary rule that satisfies "engine stays pure": `getLlmClient()` reads env and lives in `lib/llm`; the engine receives it as `deps.llm` and never imports it. Tests pass a fake.

```ts
// lib/engine/types.ts
export type Criterion = { id: string; text: string }
export type Verdict = 'prove' | 'refuse'
export interface LlmClient {
  complete(a: { system: string; prompt: string; json?: boolean }): Promise<string>
}
export type EngineEvent =
  | { type: 'criteria_parsed'; criteria: Criterion[] }
  | { type: 'criterion_start'; id: string }
  | { type: 'evidence'; id: string; pass: 1 | 2; found: boolean; cite?: string }
  | { type: 'criterion_resolved'; id: string; verdict: Verdict; rationale: string }
  | { type: 'packet_ready'; packet: unknown }

// lib/engine/index.ts  — NO next/*, NO process.env
import type { EngineEvent, LlmClient } from './types'
export async function* runEngine(
  input: { policy: string; chart: string },
  deps: { llm: LlmClient; maxCriteria?: number },
): AsyncGenerator<EngineEvent> {
  let criteria = await parseCriteria(input.policy, deps.llm)
  if (deps.maxCriteria) criteria = criteria.slice(0, deps.maxCriteria) // demo cap
  yield { type: 'criteria_parsed', criteria }
  for (const c of criteria) {
    yield { type: 'criterion_start', id: c.id }
    const [a, b] = await Promise.all([            // two independent passes, parallel
      findEvidence(c, input.chart, deps.llm),
      findEvidence(c, input.chart, deps.llm),
    ])
    yield { type: 'evidence', id: c.id, pass: 1, found: a.found, cite: a.cite }
    yield { type: 'evidence', id: c.id, pass: 2, found: b.found, cite: b.cite }
    const d = decide(a, b)
    yield { type: 'criterion_resolved', id: c.id, verdict: d.verdict, rationale: d.why }
  }
  yield { type: 'packet_ready', packet: assemble(/* collected */) }
}
```

---

## 2. Server-side run + live streaming

Use a **Route Handler returning a `ReadableStream`, framed as Server-Sent Events**, not a Server Action. **[DOC]** route handlers stream by returning `new Response(stream)` where `stream` is a `ReadableStream`, and the docs show exactly the async-iterator-to-stream pattern (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route, "Streaming"). Server Actions are RPC-style and return a single buffered result; React can stream action values via `createStreamableValue` (AI SDK), but that couples you to React internals. A route handler + SSE is portable, needs no extra dependency, and lets a plain `fetch` reader fill the matrix **[INF — portability/dependency judgment]**.

Why SSE over `EventSource`: `EventSource` is GET-only. PriorProof POSTs a `caseId` (and could POST a whole chart), so consume the stream with `fetch` + `response.body.getReader()` instead **[INF]**.

```ts
// app/api/run/route.ts
export const runtime = 'nodejs'   // LLM SDKs + maxDuration export + fluid-compute budget  [DOC]
export const maxDuration = 300    // seconds; see §4 for why 300 is the safe ceiling          [DOC]

import { runEngine } from '@/lib/engine'
import { getLlmClient } from '@/lib/llm/client'
import { loadCase } from '@/lib/fixtures'

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { caseId } = await req.json()
  const input = loadCase(caseId)
  const llm = getLlmClient()                     // reads OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  const enc = new TextEncoder()

  const stream = new ReadableStream({
    async start(controller) {
      const send = (event: string, data: unknown) =>
        controller.enqueue(enc.encode(`event: ${event}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(data)}\n\n`))
      // heartbeat: docs warn HTTP/1.1 intermediaries can drop an idle connection  [DOC]
      const hb = setInterval(() => controller.enqueue(enc.encode(`: ping\n\n`)), 15000)
      try {
        for await (const ev of runEngine(input, { llm, maxCriteria: 12 })) send(ev.type, ev)
        send('done', { ok: true })
      } catch (err) {
        send('error', { message: (err as Error).message })
      } finally {
        clearInterval(hb)
        controller.close()
      }
    },
  })

  return new Response(stream, {
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8',
      'Cache-Control': 'no-cache, no-transform',   // no-transform discourages proxy buffering [INF]
      'Connection': 'keep-alive',
      'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no',                    // belt-and-suspenders against buffering     [INF]
    },
  })
}
```

Client (a `'use client'` component) — the matrix fills as each `criterion_resolved` arrives:

```ts
// components/CoverageMatrix.tsx (excerpt)
async function runCase(caseId: string, onEvent: (e: {event: string; data: any}) => void) {
  const res = await fetch('/api/run', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ caseId }),
  })
  const reader = res.body!.getReader()
  const dec = new TextDecoder()
  let buf = ''
  for (;;) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read()
    if (done) break
    buf += dec.decode(value, { stream: true })
    const frames = buf.split('\n\n'); buf = frames.pop() ?? ''
    for (const f of frames) {
      const event = f.match(/^event: (.*)$/m)?.[1]
      const data  = f.match(/^data: (.*)$/m)?.[1]
      if (!event || !data) continue          // skip ": ping" heartbeats
      onEvent({ event, data: JSON.parse(data) })
    }
  }
}
// setState on each event → React re-renders the row for that criterion id → live fill
```

## 3. Env vars on Vercel (server-only secrets)

Any variable **without** the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix is server-only and never enters the browser bundle **[DOC — Next.js env var semantics]**. So `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` stay secret by simply not prefixing them. Never read them in a `'use client'` file; read them only in `lib/llm/client.ts` and the route handler.

Setting them with the CLI (project already linked, authenticated as zkasuran) **[DOC — https://vercel.com/docs/cli/env, updated 2026-08-20]**:

```bash
# interactive (prompts for the value, hides it from shell history)
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production
vercel env add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY production      # optional provider
vercel env add NEATLOGS_API_KEY production

# non-interactive, explicitly a Secret, no prompt
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production --sensitive --value "sk-..." --yes

# from a file as the value (keeps the secret out of bash history — preferred over `echo |`)
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production < ./openai.key

vercel env ls                                     # verify what is set, per environment
```

Add to `preview` too if you demo from a preview URL. Production vars default to type `secret` **[DOC]**. The docs explicitly warn that `echo value | vercel env add` saves the value in bash history, so use the interactive prompt or `< file` for keys **[DOC]**.

For local dev, pull them into an untracked file **[DOC]**:
```bash
vercel env pull .env.local            # development env by default
```

## 4. Timeout limits and keeping the agent under them

**[DOC — https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/duration, updated 2026-08-24]**, with Fluid compute (enabled by default on new projects):

| Plan | Default | Maximum | Extended |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hobby | 300s | **300s (5 min)** | — |
| Pro | 300s | **800s** | 1800s (30 min), beta |
| Enterprise | 300s | 800s | 1800s, beta |

Configured in App Router with the named export `export const maxDuration = 300` in the route file **[DOC]**.

**[FLAG]** these numbers assume Fluid compute is on (it is the default). If Fluid compute is disabled on the project, the older/shorter serverless limits apply and the agent can get cut off mid-run. Confirm Fluid compute is on in Project → Settings before the demo.

The limit that bites a live demo is the Hobby 300s ceiling, plus the docs' own warning that **idle** HTTP/1.1 connections can be dropped by intermediaries. Mitigations, in priority order:

1. **Stream incrementally (primary).** TTFB is tiny because `criteria_parsed` emits almost immediately and every `criterion_resolved` is pushed the instant it resolves. The matrix is visibly filling long before the function would ever hit its ceiling, so even a slow total run reads as "working," not "hung."
2. **Heartbeat every ~15s** (`: ping` comment frames) so an idle stretch between LLM calls does not look idle to the network **[DOC rationale]**.
3. **Cap criteria** for the demo (`maxCriteria: 12`). Bounds worst-case wall-clock.
4. **Parallelize the two evidence passes** per criterion with `Promise.all` (already in the sketch) to roughly halve per-criterion latency.
5. **Per-call timeout + global budget [INF].** Give each LLM call an `AbortController` timeout (e.g. 25s) and track a soft budget; if the budget is nearly spent, emit remaining criteria as a `deferred` verdict rather than blocking past the function ceiling.
6. Keep `runtime='nodejs'`. Edge runtime has different, shorter constraints and the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs expect Node **[INF; I did not pull exact Edge limits — [FLAG]]**.

Set a project-wide default in `vercel.json` if you prefer not to annotate each route **[DOC]**:
```json
{ "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "functions": { "app/api/**/*": { "maxDuration": 300 } } }
```

## 5. Content-Security-Policy and security headers (Next production)

landing.md's Vite plugin does not apply. The Next-native approach is a **nonce-based CSP generated per request in the proxy/middleware file**, with the static (non-nonce) headers in `next.config`. **[DOC — https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy, Next 16.4.0]**

**[FLAG — file name is version-dependent]** On **Next 16** the file is **`proxy.ts`** exporting `proxy()` (this is what `create-next-app` scaffolds in Oct 2026, and what the current docs show). On **Next 13.4–15** it is **`middleware.ts`** exporting `middleware()`, with an identical body. Rename the file and the function; nothing else changes.

**Tradeoff to accept consciously [DOC]:** a nonce forces **dynamic rendering** on every page (no static optimization, no CDN caching, PPR incompatible), because the nonce is injected during SSR from the request's CSP header. For PriorProof this is fine, the app is an interactive live demo, not a cacheable marketing page. If you later need the landing page statically cached, the alternative is Next's experimental hash-based CSP via Subresource Integrity (`experimental.sri`) which keeps static generation **[DOC]**.

```ts
// proxy.ts  (Next 16;  rename to middleware.ts / middleware() on <=15)
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'

export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64')
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'
  const csp = `
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ''};
    style-src 'self' ${isDev ? "'unsafe-inline'" : `'nonce-${nonce}'`};
    img-src 'self' blob: data:;
    font-src 'self';
    connect-src 'self';
    object-src 'none';
    base-uri 'self';
    form-action 'self';
    frame-ancestors 'none';
    upgrade-insecure-requests;
  `.replace(/\s{2,}/g, ' ').trim()

  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers)
  requestHeaders.set('x-nonce', nonce)
  requestHeaders.set('Content-Security-Policy', csp)
  const res = NextResponse.next({ request: { headers: requestHeaders } })
  res.headers.set('Content-Security-Policy', csp)
  return res
}

export const config = {
  matcher: [{
    source: '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)',
    missing: [
      { type: 'header', key: 'next-router-prefetch' },
      { type: 'header', key: 'purpose', value: 'prefetch' },
    ],
  }],
}
```

Notes: `connect-src 'self'` explicitly allows the same-origin `fetch('/api/run')` stream (it would also fall back to `default-src 'self'`). The matcher deliberately excludes `/api`, so the CSP's nonce machinery never touches the SSE endpoint (which returns `text/event-stream`, not HTML) — correct. Next auto-attaches the nonce to its own framework scripts and to `<Script nonce={nonce}>` read via `headers()` **[DOC]**.

Static headers (apply to every response including `/api` and static assets) go in `next.config` — do **not** also put CSP here, to avoid a conflicting second policy:

```ts
// next.config.ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
const securityHeaders = [
  { key: 'X-Content-Type-Options', value: 'nosniff' },
  { key: 'Referrer-Policy', value: 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' },
  { key: 'X-Frame-Options', value: 'DENY' },                 // legacy clickjacking fallback; frame-ancestors 'none' is the modern one in the CSP
  { key: 'Strict-Transport-Security', value: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' },
  { key: 'Permissions-Policy', value: 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), browsing-topics=()' },
  { key: 'X-DNS-Prefetch-Control', value: 'off' },
]
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  async headers() {
    return [{ source: '/:path*', headers: securityHeaders }]
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```

**[INF]** HSTS `preload` is only appropriate once you are certain the apex and all subdomains are HTTPS-only; on a throwaway `*.vercel.app` demo you may drop `preload`. Vercel serves HTTPS and sets HSTS on its own domains anyway.

# PriorProof — frontend spec

Next.js App Router on Vercel. Light and dark both first-class. Site split by category into real routes, never one scroll. House outward-words throughout.

Signature idea, stated once so every page inherits it: **a criterion is green only if a span in the chart proves it. Everything else comes back red as a named gap. The engine cannot green a row it cannot cite.**

---

## 1. Category taxonomy (decided before components)

Four categories in the top bar plus one primary action. Each category opens a hover submenu (also focus, also tap) with a one-line description per item.

**Product** — what it does and the pieces it produces.
- Overview — Prove each criterion or return it as a named gap. (→ `/`)
- Coverage matrix — Every criterion goes green with a cited span or stays red.
- The packet — The cover letter, criteria table and citations a reviewer accepts.
- Refusal by design — Why it never greens a criterion it cannot cite.

**Policies** — the real public inputs and the no-PHI charts.
- Policy library — Real public payer medical-necessity policies, split into criteria.
- Synthetic charts — No-PHI charts, the only patient data we touch.
- Coverage map — Which drugs, procedures and payers run today.

**Reports** — the required trust category.
- Metrics — Proven rate, refusal rate, citation integrity, time per packet.
- Methodology — How it decides a criterion is proven, step by step.
- Validation — The labeled set we test on and the current scores.
- Honesty and limits — What it will not do and where a human signs off.

**Developers** — the required integration category.
- Integration — Every run streams to neatlogs. Chart and policy data via Entire.
- API — One call in, a packet plus a coverage matrix out.
- Engine — Plan, retrieve, cite, refuse. The loop under the matrix.
- Docs — Quickstart, schema and the self-host guide.

**Primary action (right end of nav):** `Run the demo` → `/demo`. Theme toggle sits beside it.

Why four: Product and Policies carry the what, Reports and Developers are the two the recipe mandates get their own clean space. Green and red are status colors only, never navigation or brand, so the one-accent rule still holds (accent is blue).

---

## 2. Routes and what each page holds

```
/                        Home. Product-first hero plus scannable proof sections.
/demo                    Live engine. Pick a policy and a chart, run it, watch the matrix, build the packet.
/product/matrix          The coverage matrix explained with a static worked example.
```

- Empty: a centered card, `No policies loaded yet.` plus `Add a policy` pointing at the docs.
- Loading: a grid of card skeletons matching the real card size, no layout shift on load.
- Error (fetch failed): an inline banner, `Could not load the library.` plus `Retry`, the rest of the page intact.

**`/policies/[slug]`.**
- Bad or unknown slug: a 404 segment, `No policy by that name.` plus a link back to `/policies`. Validate the slug pattern before any fetch.

**Reports charts.**
- Empty or data-missing: the chart frame holds its size and shows `No validation data for this cut.` rather than collapsing.
- Loading: a sized placeholder equal to the final chart, no reflow.

## 6. Designed empty, loading and error states

**Coverage Matrix (home and demo).**
- Empty: before a run, rows show as muted pending skeletons with the criteria labels visible and the trace rail dim, plus a one-line `Pick a policy and a chart to run.`
- Loading: trace steps stream in accent, matrix rows carry a shimmer in the status cell, the outcome bar reads `Running`. Timeout at a few seconds via `AbortController`.
- Error (engine failed): the matrix is replaced by a bordered panel, icon in `--gap`, `The engine could not finish this run.` plus a `Try again` button that re-runs the same inputs. The header, menu and rest of the page stay up.

**Refusal is not an error.** A fully-resolved matrix with a red row is a success state. It renders in `--proven-bg` for the greens and `--gap-bg` for the one gap, with the action block, never the error panel.

**`/policies` and `/charts` lists.**
- Empty: a centered card, `No policies loaded yet.` plus `Add a policy` pointing at the docs.
- Loading: a grid of card skeletons matching the real card size, no layout shift on load.
- Error (fetch failed): an inline banner, `Could not load the library.` plus `Retry`, the rest of the page intact.

**`/policies/[slug]`.**
- Bad or unknown slug: a 404 segment, `No policy by that name.` plus a link back to `/policies`. Validate the slug pattern before any fetch.

**Reports charts.**
- Empty or data-missing: the chart frame holds its size and shows `No validation data for this cut.` rather than collapsing.
- Loading: a sized placeholder equal to the final chart, no reflow.

**Global.**
- An `error.tsx` boundary per routed segment, keyed on the route so navigation resets it. One broken page never blanks the header or the menu.
- Offline or relay-down: a dismissible top strip, `You are offline. The demo runs on canned data.` and the home hero widget still plays since it needs no network.
- Every `localStorage` read (theme, last demo inputs) is wrapped, shape-checked and capped. A tampered value falls back to the system default rather than throwing.

## 1. Install the CLI (confirmed from docs)

Linux (your platform) and the general-purpose path:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
# nightly channel: curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
entire version   # verify
```

macOS alternative (Homebrew 6.0.10+):
```bash
brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
```

From Go source (needs Go 1.27.1+, this is the only path that needs Go; packaged installs bundle their own runtime):
```bash
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/git-remote-entire@latest
export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
```

The CLI is MIT-licensed and open source (repo github.com/entireio/cli).

Prerequisites (confirmed): Git installed and configured; a GitHub account with an accessible repo; an AI coding agent installed (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.); macOS/Linux/Windows. Optional: the `gh` CLI if you want to create a demo repo from the terminal. A C compiler is NOT required for the standard prebuilt installs; the hackathon page mentions a C compiler only for building Brain/Graph tree-sitter bindings from source, which you avoid by using the prebuilt installers.

Important mechanism (confirmed): Entire works by installing git hooks plus agent hooks in your repo. It captures your AI coding-agent SESSION and links it to a git COMMIT. That pairing is a checkpoint. This is a development-time tool that records how the code was built; it is not a runtime state store for your own deployed agent (this matters for your PriorProof design, see section 5).

## 2. Authenticate and connect GitHub

### Interactive vs headless (confirmed from the CLI README)

Login command: `entire login`.
- Default: opens a browser, sign in with GitHub, tokens stored in the OS keyring. This is the OAuth/browser step and must be done by the human.
- Headless box with a browser elsewhere: `entire login --device` forces a device-code flow (it also falls back to this automatically when no local browser). A human still has to open the shown URL and enter the code once.
- File-backed token storage instead of keyring: `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file entire login` writes `tokens.json` at mode 0600 (path overridable via `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`).
- Fully non-interactive / CI: `ENTIRE_TOKEN=<JWT> entire ...` injects a login-or-service-account session token per invocation, bypasses stored creds, writes nothing to disk. `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` exists for checkpoint-repo git operations.
- Account management: `entire auth status`, `entire auth switch`, `entire auth token`; `entire logout`.

### GitHub App + repo connection (confirmed)

Two separate things authenticate you: (1) `entire login` for the CLI, and (2) the Entire GitHub App, which must be installed and granted access to the repo. Nothing repo-related shows on entire.io until the GitHub App is installed and the repo imported. Access then mirrors the GitHub collaborator list (no separate invites). Sync "can take up to an hour."

CLI mirror flow (connect an existing GitHub repo to Entire's network):
```bash
entire login
entire repo mirror add
entire repo remote add entire      # adds an 'entire' git remote
git remote -v
git fetch entire
git push entire
# optional, repoint origin at the mirror:
# entire repo remote add origin --override
```

What is scriptable headlessly: install, `entire enable -y`, mirror add, remote add, all git push/commit, `entire checkpoint ...`, Graph and Brain install/setup. CI auth via `ENTIRE_TOKEN`.
What needs a human with a browser (once): the first `entire login` (or the device-code entry) and authorizing the Entire GitHub App on the `zkasuran` account and granting it the `priorproof` repo. Org-owned repos need an org admin to approve the app.

```bash
# ...run your coding agent, make a focused change...

# Entire prompts at commit time: "Link this commit to session context? [Y]es/[n]o/[a]lways"
```

  For you: `https://entire.io/gh/zkasuran/priorproof/commit/<SHA>`. The page shows Sessions (prompt, transcript, tool calls) and Changes (diffs) tabs.
